subject: Critical Thinking
title: Superforecasting: What the Best Predictors Do Differently
description: A 60-second lesson on Superforecasting: What the Best Predictors Do Differently.

hook.text: Philip Tetlock's 20-year study: most expert predictions are barely better than chance.

buildup.text: Superforecasters: ordinary people who outperform intelligence analysts with classified data.

discovery.text: Key traits: they update often, think in probabilities, consider many perspectives, & distinguish what they know from.

twist.text: Hedgehogs perform worst. Foxes perform best. Intellectual humility wins.

climax.text: Anyone can improve: keep a prediction journal, track accuracy, and calibrate. It's a trainable skill, not a gift.

punchline.text: The best forecasters aren't smarter. They're more humble and more precise.

quiz.question: What distinguishes superforecasters from average experts?
options: They think in probabilities, update often, and show intellectual humility

details.summary: Philip Tetlock's research identified 'superforecasters' who consistently outperform experts and even intelligence analysts. They think probabilistically, update frequently, and keep score of their accuracy.
details.whyItMatters: Superforecasting shows that prediction accuracy is a skill that can be learned, not an innate gift. The methods are accessible to anyone willing to practice.
takeaways: Superforecasters are foxes who know many things, not hedgehogs
They update beliefs incrementally with new evidence
Keeping precise track of accuracy drives rapid improvement

faq.question: What habits do superforecasters practice that ordinary people do not?
faq.answer: They assign numerical probabilities, break questions into sub-components, seek diverse information sources, update predictions frequently, and hold themselves accountable by tracking accuracy. Most people do none of these things.

faq.question: Can anyone become a superforecaster with enough practice?
faq.answer: Tetlock's research suggests that open-mindedness, intellectual curiosity, and willingness to update beliefs matter more than raw intelligence. With deliberate practice, most people can significantly improve their forecasting accuracy.
